forms: pick the word from its description
say what a compound is made of
sort substances into elements and compounds
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.mastery: The child says an atom is the smallest particle of an element, an element is made of one kind of atom (oxygen, iron), a molecule is two or more atoms joined (water, oxygen gas) and a compound is made of different elements joined chemically (water, salt). The child does not say a compound is a mixture or an atom is a molecule. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the symbol of an element
pick the element of a symbol
say how a symbol is written
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.mastery: The child gives the symbols H (hydrogen), O (oxygen), C (carbon), N (nitrogen), S (sulphur), Na (sodium), K (potassium), Ca (calcium), Mg (magnesium), Fe (iron), Cu (copper), Zn (zinc), Al (aluminium), Cl (chlorine), Ag (silver) and Au (gold), writes a capital first letter and a small second letter, and does not give the first letter of the name for iron, sodium or potassium. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the word equation
name the product
put the reactants and product in order
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.mastery: The child writes a word equation with the reactants first, an arrow and the product (magnesium + oxygen gives magnesium oxide; iron + sulphur gives iron sulphide; hydrogen + oxygen gives water; carbon + oxygen gives carbon dioxide; sodium + chlorine gives sodium chloride), names the compound from the elements (an oxide from oxygen, a sulphide from sulphur, a chloride from chlorine), and does not put the product first. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the use of an element
pick the element for a use
say what a label tells
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.mastery: The child says copper is used for electric wires, iron for tools and nails, aluminium for cooking pots and foil, carbon for charcoal and pencils, nitrogen in fertilisers, chlorine to make water safe and oxygen for breathing, and that a packaging label tells the contents, the amounts and the dates to use it by. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the particle picture of a state
say how close the particles are
say how the particles move
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..mastery: The child says the particles of a solid are close together in fixed places and only vibrate, the particles of a liquid are close but slide past each other, and the particles of a gas are far apart and move freely in all directions, and does not say solid particles do not move. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what pure water does
say what salt does to the boiling point
say what an impurity does to the melting point
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..mastery: The child says a pure substance melts and boils at fixed temperatures (pure water melts at 0 degrees Celsius and boils at 100), that impurities raise the boiling point and lower the melting point (salty water boils above 100 degrees and freezes below 0), and does not say impurities lower the boiling point. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: sort a change
say what a new substance shows
pick a use of a change of state
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..mastery: The child says a physical change makes no new substance and can usually be reversed (melting ice, dissolving sugar, boiling water), a chemical change makes a new substance and is usually not reversible (burning wood, rusting iron, cooking an egg, milk going sour), and does not call burning physical or melting chemical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the parts of the fire triangle
say which part to remove
pick a cause of fire in nature
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.mastery: The child says a fire needs heat, fuel and oxygen, that taking away any one puts the fire out (cooling with water removes heat, a blanket removes oxygen, clearing dry grass removes fuel), names natural causes (lightning, volcanic eruptions, dry grass lit by the hot sun) and does not say fire needs only heat and fuel. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick what puts out a wood fire
pick what to use on an oil fire
say what to do about an electrical fire
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.mastery: The child says water suits a fire of wood, paper or cloth, that an oil or petrol fire is smothered with sand, a blanket or foam and never put out with water, that an electrical fire needs the power switched off and a dry powder or carbon dioxide extinguisher and never water, and that the first step is to raise the alarm and keep safe. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the part from its job
pick the part only plant cells have
compare plant and animal cells
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.CELL_PARTS.mastery: The child says both cells have a cell membrane (controls what enters and leaves), cytoplasm (where reactions happen) and a nucleus (controls the cell), and that plant cells also have a cell wall (supports the cell), chloroplasts (make food with light) and a large vacuole (stores sap), and does not give an animal cell a cell wall or a chloroplast. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: calculate the total magnification
say what the eyepiece and objective do
pick the units
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.mastery: The child multiplies the magnification of the eyepiece and the objective lens (10 times 40 gives 400 times), says each lens magnifies and the total is the product, and does not add the two numbers or use only the objective. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the process from a description
say which way particles move
say what diffusion or osmosis does in a living thing
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..mastery: The child says diffusion is the spreading of particles from where there are many to where there are few until they are even, osmosis is the movement of water through a thin membrane from a weak solution to a stronger one, gives examples (the smell of cooking, the uptake of water by root hairs, oxygen entering blood), and says neither needs energy from the cell. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say how long the cycle is
say when an egg is released
pick a healthy way to manage cramps or bleeding
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..mastery: The child says the cycle is about 28 days, the bleeding (menstruation) lasts about three to seven days, an egg is released about the middle of the cycle (ovulation), the cycle is normal and not an illness, and picks healthy ways to cope (clean pads or cloths changed often, bathing, rest, warm drinks, talking to a trusted adult and seeing a health worker for severe pain). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: put the events in order
say where fertilisation happens
say what the zygote is
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..mastery: The child says fertilisation is a sperm joining an egg in the oviduct to make a zygote, the zygote divides as it travels to the uterus, and implantation is the embryo attaching to the wall of the uterus, and puts the events in that order. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a symptom of an STI
pick a way an STI is NOT spread
pick a prevention measure
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..mastery: The child names STIs (HIV, syphilis, gonorrhoea, chlamydia), symptoms (unusual discharge, pain when passing urine, sores, itching), knows they are not spread by hugging, shaking hands or toilet seats, and picks prevention (abstinence, faithfulness to one uninfected partner, not sharing needles or razors, testing and treatment, going to a health worker). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the form of energy
sort a source
pick a Kenyan source
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..mastery: The child names forms (kinetic, potential, heat, light, sound, electrical, chemical), sorts renewable sources (the sun, wind, flowing water, geothermal, biogas) from non-renewable ones (coal, petroleum, natural gas), and knows Kenya uses geothermal (Olkaria), hydro and wind (Lake Turkana) power. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the transformation
pick what a device changes energy into
pick the safety measure
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..mastery: The child says energy changes form and is never created or used up (an electric kettle changes electrical energy to heat, a solar panel light to electrical, a lamp electrical to light, falling water potential to kinetic to electrical, a burning match chemical to heat and light) and picks safety measures (do not touch bare wires, keep flammable things away from heat, ask an adult). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the way to increase pressure
calculate the pressure from the force and the area
say how liquid pressure changes with depth
find the false step in a learner's reason
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.mastery: The child says pressure is the force on each unit of area, so the same force on a smaller area makes a bigger pressure (a sharp knife, a nail) and on a larger area a smaller pressure (wide tyres, snow shoes), calculates pressure as force divided by area, and says liquid pressure grows with depth (a dam wall is thicker at the bottom). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
